steps.path: Any command the assistant runs that needs admin rights
steps.headline: This is what done means for the admin password card.

rows.statement: You type your admin password inside the chat card itself, never a separate system pop-up.
Approving an admin command and entering your password are two separate steps, not one combined action.
The password card can appear after a command has already started, naming the exact step that needs admin rights.
This first version covers only your computer's admin password; other logins (keys, GitHub, SSH) are separate, later projects.
After each admin command finishes, the app makes your computer forget the password, so the next admin step asks again.
Typing your admin password from a paired phone or browser is allowed, with its leftover risks accepted.
When 'sudo' is visibly written in the command, the password is asked right after approval, before anything runs.
Every mode's admin-command card shows the exact command, matches the Full auto stop's look, and has no Always Allow or text below the buttons.
Your password box spans the card, with a show/hide eye and a small Confirm button built into its right side; Enter also confirms.
A wrong password shows a yellow warning banner saying how many tries remain, and clears the box for your next try.
Before your last try, the same yellow banner warns that another wrong password may lock you out of admin actions for about 10 minutes.
When a script asks for your password partway through, a highlighted box names the script and says to type only if you expected it.
A command still running with admin rights shows a 'Running as admin' strip with how long it's run and a Stop button, even when folded.
Your admin password is never saved, never shown to the assistant, and never written into chat history.
The password card's wording is always the app's own, never text a command supplies.
Your password is only ever handed to your computer's genuine admin program, never to something faking it.
Full auto still stops for every admin command, and a helper's admin request shows on your card labeled with its name.
Three wrong passwords in a row can lock you out of admin actions for about 10 minutes, and you're warned before the last try.
Every step waits for you with no time limit; the approval card's Skip, or closing the session, stops the command.
This is for Mac and Linux; Windows keeps its own pop-up and phones still can't run admin commands.
